sections.heading: Downloads
sections.html: Patterns download as print-at-home PDFs with a one-inch test square, plus the copy-shop file on 36-inch paper. Whatever you download while subscribed stays in your account forever, including after you cancel.

sections.title: Plans and licensing
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: One quilter, a whole guild, or a shop that wants the retreat programs handled.

sections.heading: How the subscription works
sections.html: One plan, billed monthly, every pattern included. Sell quilts from the patterns at any scale that does not involve a factory. Guild plans cover retreat programs and workshops; shop plans cover teaching. Open the membership form to start the free month.

items.q: Can I sell quilts made from the patterns?
items.a: Yes, small-batch and handmade. The one line in the sand is mass production, which no subscriber has ever had the equipment for anyway.

items.q: Do I keep downloads if I cancel?
items.a: Yes. Everything in your account stays downloaded and yours. The drawer just stops opening to new patterns.
Yes: it covers printing patterns for workshops and retreats up to fifty members a year, which is most guilds and both of the big ones.

sections.heading: Members choose the month
sections.html: Each month the draft list goes to a member vote, which is why the drawer contains an entire surprising section of feed-sack reproductions and one very popular basket pattern with questionable instructions for the handle. Democracy holds.

sections.title: About {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Three pattern designers, one tester list of two hundred, and a shared belief that instructions should never say simply quilt as desired.

sections.html:
The drawer began as a shared folder between three designers who were tired of writing the same yardage charts separately. The folder became a catalog, the catalog became a subscription, and the subscription funded the testing list, which is the real product: two hundred quilters sew every pattern before it is published.

Patterns that fail testing get fixed or filed, and the fixes are posted free to everyone who owns the pattern, which is the entire business model wearing a cardigan.

items.quote: Their instructions include the seam you are about to sew wrong. I have never felt so understood by a PDF.
